angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 629,609 km at 199.58 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0105 +/- 0.0154 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 199.58 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.905 +/- 0.035 solar radii from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract): 629,609 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.94 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5373 +/- 100 K from Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Howard et al. 2025, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-105.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.498, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
